land.text: the province of Tashir, granted to Kiurike by his brother Smbat II in 979
Lori and Agarak, captured and annexed by David IV in 1118

successors.note: The Kiurikid line kept the royal title until the Mongol conquest in the early 13th century (Tashir-Dzoraget page).

capitals.name: Matsnaberd
capitals.note: Infobox gives Matsnaberd 979-1065; the text says Kiurike II moved the capital to Lori in 1064. Coordinates approximate (Tashir district, Lori).

capitals.name: Lori (Lori Berd)
capitals.note: Infobox 'Lori (1065-1118)'; the text dates the move 1064.

correction.text: the province of Tashir and Dzoraget, in 'modern northern Armenia, northwestern Azerbaijan, and southern Georgia'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, 979-1117. The page places the kingdom in northern Armenia, north-western Azerbaijan and southern Georgia and gives no area and no boundary; Lori province is the reading shared with the Bagratid Armenia and Kingdom of Georgia dossiers, and the Azerbaijani and Georgian parts are not drawn. David I Anhoghin's conquests from the Emirates of Tbilisi and Ganja are undated and not drawn.

ledger.note: 979: Smbat II grants Tashir to his brother Kiurike with the title of king, founding the Kingdom of Tashir-Dzoraget. 'In 979 King Smbat II of Armenia granted the province of Tashir to his brother Kiurike with the title of king'; infobox 'Established: 979'.
1064: Kiurike II moves the capital from Matsnaberd to Lori. 'Kiurike II moved the capital from Matsnaberd to Lori in 1064' (infobox 'Lori (1065-1118)').
1118: David IV takes Lori. 'Still in 1118, the Armenian towns of Lori and Agarak were captured by David IV' (the Tashir-Dzoraget page: annexed to the Kingdom of Georgia in 1118).

region.text: the Kiurikid kingdom, annexed by Georgia

ledger.note: 1118: Tashir-Dzoraget is annexed to the Kingdom of Georgia. The page: Kiurike's line 'ruled until 1118 when Tashir-Dzoraget was annexed to the Kingdom of Georgia'.

wars.name: Revolt of David I Anhoghin
wars.outcome: David I Anhoghin 'unsuccessfully tried to gain independence from the Bagratid kings'; Gagik I took his possessions, which earned David the name Anhoghin (landless).
wars.note: Undated territorial effect: David reigned 989-1048 and the kingdom continued, so the page's loss is not drawn.

wars.name: David IV's capture of Lori
wars.outcome: David IV captured Lori and Agarak in 1118 and annexed Tashir-Dzoraget.
wars.note: The Tashir-Dzoraget page does not mention David IV by name.

certainty.note: The page gives no boundary; Lori province stands in for the Tashir and Dzoraget districts.

sources.title: Kingdom of Tashir-Dzoraget
sources.note: Founding 979, capital move 1064, David I Anhoghin 1001, Kiurike II 1045-1048, annexation 1118; no area.

notes: No Cliopatria row. Undated statements on the Tashir-Dzoraget page and left out of the ledger: David I Anhoghin 'conquered some territories from Emirates of Tbilisi and Ganja' (reign 989-1048), the kingdom 'became suzerain of the Emirate of Tiflis' at its peak, held sway over Kakheti-Hereti (a branch ruled there 1029-1105, which the Kakheti-Hereti dossier does not mention), and Kiurike II 'became a vassal of the Seljuk Empire' in the Seljuk invasions. After 1045 the Bagratid dossier ends Tashir-Dzoraget's vassalage (vassal_end 1045 with counterpart kingdom-of-tashir-dzoraget); the Tashir page has Kiurike II receive Byzantine recognition then (reign 1048-1089). The page does not mention the Shaddadids or David IV. Sizing: no page gives an area, so no area comparison was possible (Lori province resolves to about 3,800 km2 on the gazetteer). wikidata null.
